# What is Photon?
Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/photon
Fetched: 2026-06-16
Last updated on page: Jun 16, 2026

## What is Photon?
"The Databricks-native vectorized query engine that accelerates your SQL workloads, DataFrame API calls, ETL pipelines, and stateless streaming workloads."
"Up to 5x better price/performance for data and analytics workloads" (TPC-DS benchmarks vs competing cloud warehouses).

## How Photon works
Replaces "the JVM-based Spark SQL execution engine with a native C++ runtime" for supported operations.
"Processes data in columnar batches rather than row by row" — enables SIMD instruction utilization across thousands of rows simultaneously.
"When Photon encounters an unsupported operation during query execution, it transparently falls back to the Spark runtime for the remainder of that operation."

## Performance optimizations
- Hash joins replacing sort-merge joins
- Native Parquet writer for Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Parquet writes (supports UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE INTO, INSERT, CTAS)
- Filter pushdown and dictionary pruning reducing storage reads

## Integration with Databricks platform
Enabled by default on: serverless compute, SQL warehouses.

## Photon enablement
Classic compute: Use Photon Acceleration checkbox under Performance.
API (cluster/jobs): set `runtime_engine` to `PHOTON`.
API (pipelines): set `photon` to `true`.

## Features that require Photon enablement
- Predictive IO (read and write)
- Dynamic file pruning in MERGE, UPDATE, and DELETE statements

## Supported instance types
Photon supports a number of instance types including Graviton-based instances.
"Photon instance types consume DBUs at a different rate" (see Databricks pricing page).

## Supported operators, expressions, and data types
Operators: Scan, Filter, Project, Hash Aggregate, Hash Join, Hash Shuffle, Window Functions, Sorts.
Data types: numeric, string, date/timestamp, struct, array, map, geometry, geography.

## Monitor Photon usage
Spark UI: Photon operators shown in orange within the query DAG.
Query profile (SQL warehouses / serverless): Photon operators shown in purple; standard operators in grey.

## Limitations
- Queries completing in under 2 seconds: no meaningful improvement.
- UDFs (User Defined Functions): not supported.
- RDD APIs: not supported.
- Dataset APIs: not supported.
- Stateful streaming: not supported.
- Graviton + Photon: "Graviton-based instances with Photon don't support Databricks Container Services, or Databricks SQL warehouses."
